page.layout: One page of text: a Hebrew-Latin dictionary in one column of entries, with Hebrew words set among the Latin. Running head in Hebrew at top centre; page number 406 at top right. A catchword "vel" at lower right.

main_text.p: מָהַר Dotavit, Dotem constituit: Praeterit. מָהַר Dotant, Psal.16.4. Infinit. cum Futuro, יְמַהֵרֵנָּה Dotando constituet dotem ipsi, Exod.22.16. Pih. מִהֵר Festinavit, Acceleravit: 1.Sam.4.14. מִהַרְתָּ לִמְצֹא Festinasti invenire, Gen.27.20. Niph. נִמְהַר Festinanter fieri, Praecipitari: Praeter. נִמְהַר נִפְתָּלִים וְעֵצַת Consilium retortorum vel reluctantium praecipitatur, Job.5.13. id est, praeceps adeoque temerarium fit. Partic. וְהַנִּמְהָר Et festinam, praecipitem, Hab.1.6. Plural. נִמְהָרִים Praecipites, Inconsiderati, Jesa.32.4.
מָהִיר m. Promptus, Festinus, סֵפֶר מָהִיר Scriba promptus, Psalm.45.2. Constr. מְהִיר צֶדֶק Promptus ad justitiam, Jesa.16.5.
מָהִיר m. Festinus: קָרוֹב וּמָהִיר מְאֹד Propinquus & festinus valde, Soph.1.14. Et adverbialiter, Cito, Celeriter, Festinanter, Deut.7.22.

מְהִירָה f. Festinatio, Celeritas: Semper autem adverbialiter, vel praefixa Praepos. ב, vel simpliciter: בִּמְהִירָה יִנָּתֵק Cito rumpitur, Eccles.4.12. מְהִירָה קַל Leviter cito, id est, velocissime, Joel.3.4.

מוֹ Est interdum syllaba expletiva, assumens ante se litexas serviles; ut, בְּמוֹ In, Cum, Psal.11.2. לְמוֹ Ad, Job.39. v.2. כְּמוֹ Sicut, Job.12.3. quod cum Aff. כְּמוֹנִי Sicut ego, sicut tu, 1.Reg.22.4. Interdum est pro הֵם; unde, לְמוֹ Eis, pro לָהֶם Jesa.44.15.

מוּג Liquefactus, Solutus, Dissolutus fuit: Et semel activè, וַתְּמוּגֵנָה Et dissolvis nos, Jesa.64.7. Niph. נִמּוֹג Se dissolvere, Diffluere, Liquescere, Colliquescere, & metaphoricè semper usurpatur: Praeteritum, נָמֹגּוּ Diffluent, Exod.15.15. Particip. נְמוֹגִים Solvuntur, vel

page.notes: Hebrew forms are copied from a small, dense print; the vowel points and some consonants are uncertain and are not marked individually, so check the Hebrew against the scan. The Latin and Hebrew reference numbers are as printed. The entry "מוֹ" has a large initial letter and the note "Interdum est pro הֵם" is followed by a semicolon as printed. The running head is in Hebrew (two words) and the catchword "vel" is in italics at lower right. Printing errors were left as printed, such as "litexas" (for "litteras"?) and "Jesa", which is printed without a full crossbar on the f-like s.
